questions: What are the legal criteria for 3rd party software?
answer: virtualQ evaluates third-party software based on strict legal and compliance requirements focused on GDPR-aligned data privacy license compatibility IP protection and regulatory adherence. Software must ensure clear data locality secure handling and proper inclusion in DPAs. All licenses—especially open source—must allow unrestricted commercial use and not threaten virtualQ’s IP rights. Tools are checked for long-term support security (via audits Snyk) and must avoid outdated or risky components. Preference is given to portable industry-standard technologies to prevent vendor lock-in.

questions: Which programming languages do we use?
answer: The virtualQ system is built using a diverse technology stack with Ruby(43%) making up the largest portion of the codebase followed by HTML/JavaScript(24%) Python(11%) .NET/C#(9%) and Elixir(7%). The remaining share consists of other technologies such as Terraform templates.

The system uses Ruby on Rails as its primary backend framework and React with Redux for the frontend. Rails handles data processing storage and API or UI interactions while React provides the component-based UI structure and Redux manages centralized application state.

questions: What are internal and external audits and how do they differ?
answer: Internal audits focus on code quality design verification and vulnerability detection using automated tools like Debricked and Snyk mainly in non-production environments. They are part of ongoing development processes. External audits performed by independent partners include penetration tests that simulate real attacks to validate the security of customer-facing systems. In essence internal audits proactively maintain code and process integrity while external audits provide independent assurance of virtualQ’s overall security posture.
